```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(arrow)
})


bkt   <- s3_bucket("mperier", endpoint_override = Sys.getenv("AWS_S3_ENDPOINT"))



INE <- setDT(read_delim_arrow(bkt$path("panel_hogares/69754.csv"),   # <- adapt the name
                              delim = ";", as_data_frame = TRUE,
                              col_types = schema(Edad = string(),
                                                 `Relación residencial entre Censos` = string(),
                                                 Nacionalidad = string(), Sexo = string(),
                                                 Periodo = string(), Total = string())))

setnames(INE, c("age", "relation", "nationality", "sex", "year", "n"))
INE[, `:=`(year = as.integer(year),
           n    = as.numeric(gsub(".", "", n, fixed = TRUE)))] 


PANEL <- setDT(read_parquet(bkt$path("panel_hogares/panel_persons_2016_2023_sec.parquet")))
cols_start <- names(PANE)
Lstopifnot(PANEL[!is.na(SECCION), all(nchar(SECCION) == 10L)])
PANEL[, DISTRITO := substr(SECCION, 1, 7)]
PANEL[, obs_prev := obs_prev %in% TRUE]
PANEL[, mun := paste0(CPRO, CMUN)]
setorder(PANEL, IDENPER, year)
```

The goal of this script is to grasp, quantify and describe residential mobility of the people & households in the panel :

We use multiple definitions of *moving* in this script the most flexible one being "change of **seccion censal"** between two years (given that this is not just a recoding of the section). Further down in this script we prefer to use the change of **district** between two years. We prefer districts because they are less likely to change between years and because it is easier to link this panel to any other database if we use the district level than the seccion censal (less common).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

PANEL[, same_id := IDENPER == shift(IDENPER)]
for (v in c("year", "SECCION", "DISTRITO", "mun", "CPRO", "IDENHOG", "hh_w")) {
  nv <- paste0(v, "_p")
  PANEL[, (nv) := shift(get(v))]
  PANEL[!(same_id %in% TRUE), (nv) := NA]
}

PANEL[, gap := year - year_p - 1L]



# D4 : obs_prev doit signifier « observé en t-1 ». Si obs_prev est vrai, la
# ligne précédente de la même personne doit être l'année t-1.
print(PANEL[, .N, by = .(obs_prev, prev_is_t1 = !is.na(year_p) & year - year_p == 1L)])
stopifnot(PANEL[obs_prev & (is.na(year_p) | year - year_p != 1L), .N] == 0)

# ---- 3. Changements bruts ----------------------------------------------------
# NA quand la section manque l'une des deux années.
PANEL[obs_prev & !is.na(SECCION) & !is.na(SECCION_p), `:=`(
  move_sec  = SECCION != SECCION_p,
  move_dist = DISTRITO != DISTRITO_p,
  move_mun  = mun     != mun_p,
  move_prov = CPRO    != CPRO_p)]

```

```{r verif recode}
#| echo: false
#| output: false


SEUIL_RECODE   <- 0.40   # part des ménages de A passés en B au-delà de laquelle A -> B est un recodage
MIN_HOG_RECODE <- 2L     # nombre minimal de ménages pour qu'une transition puisse être un recodage (D3)


# ---- 4. Recodages de sections -----------------------------------------------
# 4a. Base : nombre de ménages (de t-1) observés en t, par section d'origine.
B <- PANEL[obs_prev & !is.na(move_sec),
           .(n_hog_base = uniqueN(IDENHOG_p)), by = .(year, SECCION_p)]

# 4b. Transitions A -> B au sein d'une même municipalité (D2).
Tr <- PANEL[obs_prev & move_sec %in% TRUE & move_mun %in% FALSE,
            .(n_hog_tr = uniqueN(IDENHOG_p), n_pers_tr = .N),
            by = .(year, SECCION_p, SECCION)]
Tr <- B[Tr, on = .(year, SECCION_p)]
Tr[, share := n_hog_tr / n_hog_base]

# 4c. Règle : recodage si >= 40 % des ménages de A passent en B (et >= 2 ménages).
Tr[, recode := share >= SEUIL_RECODE & n_hog_tr >= MIN_HOG_RECODE]

# Diagnostic : combien de transitions et de ménages sont reclassés, par année.
print(Tr[, .(transitions = .N, recodages = sum(recode),
             hog_recodes = sum(n_hog_tr[recode]), hog_tous = sum(n_hog_tr)),
         by = year][order(year)])



# 4d. Report sur les personnes.
PANEL[, recode := NA]
PANEL[!is.na(move_sec), recode := FALSE]
PANEL[Tr[recode == TRUE], on = .(year, SECCION_p, SECCION), recode := TRUE]


```

Number and proportion of movers in 2017-2023

```{r move}
#| echo: false

#---- 5. Déménagement retenu ---------------------------------------------------
# move = changement de section qui n'est pas un recodage.
# Un changement de municipalité ou de province n'est jamais un recodage (D2).

PANEL[, move := move_sec & !recode]

table(PANEL$move, useNA = "ifany")
tab <- table(PANEL$move)
prop.table(tab)
```

`move` = 1 if the person’s census section changed between t−1 and t, unless the change is a recoding (same municipality, ≥ 40 % of the origin section’s households making the same transition, and at least 2 households). Changes of municipality are always counted as moves. NA if the person is not observed in t−1 or the section is missing.

Looking at the district level definition :

```{r move_dist }
#| echo: false

#---- 5. Déménagement retenu ---------------------------------------------------
# move = changement de section qui n'est pas un recodage.

table(PANEL$move_dist, useNA = "ifany")
tab <- table(PANEL$move_dist)
prop.table(tab)

```

If we tolerate a change of district between *t-2* and *t* rather than *t-1* and *t* when the person is absent of the panel in *t-1* the number and proportion of movers is very slightly higher

```{r move district extended in time }
#| echo: false


PANEL[, move_dist_ext := fcase(
  obs_prev & !is.na(move_dist),                            move_dist,
  gap == 1L & !is.na(DISTRITO) & !is.na(DISTRITO_p),       DISTRITO != DISTRITO_p,
  default = NA)]

table(PANEL$move_dist_ext, useNA="ifany")
tabdis <- table(PANEL$move_dist_ext)
prop.table(tabdis)

# Keep track of which comparison was used
PANEL[!is.na(move_dist_ext), dist_comp := fifelse(obs_prev, "t-1", "t-2")]
PANEL[, .N, by = .(year, dist_comp, move_dist_ext)][order(year, dist_comp, move_dist_ext)]
```

`move_dist_ext` = 1 if the person’s district changed between their previous observation and year t, allowing a one-year gap. If the person is observed in t−1, it equals `move_dist`(districts are assumed never recoded) : a change of district (first 7 digits of the census section code) that is not a section recoding. If the person is absent in t−1 but observed in t−2, it is the raw change of district between t−2 and t; recodings cannot be excluded in this case. NA if the person is not observed in t−1 or t−2, or if the district is missing. `dist_comp` indicates which comparison was used (“t-1” or “t-2”).

**=\> Tolerating for an extra year of interval doesn't add that much information and complicates year-level interpretation so we tend to prefer the strict definition : moving = changing district between t-1 and t**

#### Proportion of movers per year and type of moving :

```{r desc}
#| echo: false

(paste0("Number of moves (defined as district change) in the total panel :", sum(PANEL$move_dist == TRUE, na.rm=T)))

# Weighted mean ignoring NA in x and in w
wm <- function(x, w) { ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(w); sum(x[ok] * w[ok]) / sum(w[ok]) }

# Weighted move rates by year, one column per definition
rates <- PANEL[year >= 2017, .(
  n_t1     = sum(!is.na(move)),             # rows compared with t-1
  n_t2     = sum(dist_comp %in% "t-2"),     # extra rows compared with t-2 (gap)
  raw_sec  = wm(move_sec,          w),      # section change, recodes included
  move     = wm(move,              w),      # section change, recodes excluded = move rate
  dist     = wm(move_dist,     w),          # district change (districts assumed never recoded)
  dist_ext = wm(move_dist_ext,     w),      # dist + people absent in t-1 (t-2 comparison)
  mun      = wm(move_mun,          w),      # municipality change
  prov     = wm(move_prov,         w)),     # province change
  by = year][order(year)]

# Display in %
pct <- setdiff(names(rates), c("year", "n_t1", "n_t2"))
rates[, (pct) := lapply(.SD, function(x) round(100 * x, 2)), .SDcols = pct]
rates[]

```

| Variable | Definition |
|----|----|
| `n_t1` | Number of persons observed in both t−1 and t (rows used for the yearly rates) |
| `n_t2` | Number of extra persons absent in t−1 but observed in t−2, added only in `dist_ext` |
| `raw_sec` | \% of persons whose census section changed between t−1 and t, section recodings included |
| `move` | \% of persons whose census section changed between t−1 and t, recodings excluded: **the move rate** |
| `dist` | **% of persons whose district changed between t−1 and t (districts assumed never recoded)** |
| `dist_ext` | Same as `dist`, plus persons absent in t−1 compared with t−2 (two-year interval) |
| `mun` | \% of persons whose municipality changed between t−1 and t |
| `prov` | \% of persons whose province changed between t−1 and t |

#### % of movers by type of moves & age

```{r}
#| echo: false


# ---- 6. Move type (what happens to the household) ----------------------------
# Origin household (t-1):
#   h_nobs  : members of the t-1 household observed in t
#   h_nmove : how many of them moved
H <- PANEL[obs_prev & !is.na(move), .(h_nobs = .N, h_nmove = sum(move)), by = .(year, IDENHOG_p)]
PANEL[H, on = .(year, IDENHOG_p), `:=`(h_nobs = i.h_nobs, h_nmove = i.h_nmove)]

# Destination household (t): number of distinct t-1 households it is made of.
#   1  -> same people as before (or a subset): "same_group"
#   >1 -> mixed with people from another household: "with_others"
# People not observed in t-1 (newborns, entrants) are excluded from the count.
A <- PANEL[obs_prev & !is.na(move), .(n_orig = uniqueN(IDENHOG_p)), by = .(year, IDENHOG)]
PANEL[A, on = .(year, IDENHOG), arrival := fifelse(i.n_orig > 1L, "with_others", "same_group")]

# Origin type: the whole household moved (including one-person households)
# or only part of it.
PANEL[move %in% TRUE, origin := fifelse(h_nmove == h_nobs, "whole", "part")]

# 4 types: whole_same_group, whole_with_others, part_same_group, part_with_others
PANEL[move %in% TRUE, type := paste(origin, arrival, sep = "_")]
rm(H, A)

# ---- 7. Results --------------------------------------------------------------
# Weighted rates (share of people observed in t-1 and t who moved)
(PANEL[obs_prev & !is.na(move) & !is.na(w),
            .(raw_sec = weighted.mean(move_sec,  w, na.rm = TRUE),
              move    = weighted.mean(move,      w, na.rm = TRUE),
              move_dist= weighted.mean(move_dist ,      w, na.rm = TRUE), 
              mun     = weighted.mean(move_mun,  w, na.rm = TRUE),
              prov    = weighted.mean(move_prov, w, na.rm = TRUE)),
            by = year][order(year)])

# By age 
print(PANEL[obs_prev & !is.na(move_dist) & !is.na(w),
            .(move_dist = weighted.mean(move_dist, w, na.rm = TRUE)),
            by = .(age_b = cut(age, c(-1, 15, 24, 34, 44, 54, 64, 120)))][order(age_b)])

# Distribution by move type
print(PANEL[move_dist %in% TRUE, .(n = .N, w_sum = sum(w, na.rm = TRUE)), by = type][
  , share := w_sum / sum(w_sum)][order(-share)])

```

Some section changes do not correspond to families moving but to sections being recoded (when a very large share of households in a given section censal move to another section censal in the same municipality) =\> if over 40% of hh move from the same to the same censal section, we consider to be a recoding

**raw_sec** = % of moves without taking out the recodages

**move** = % of moves once the recodages taken away (seccion censal)

**move_dist** = % of moves as in district level changes

**mun / prov** = % of change of munipality / province

| origin / dest | `same_group (no newcomers)` | `with_others (with newcomers)` |
|----|----|----|
| **`whole`** (entire household, including one-person households) | the household moves as it is | the household moves in with others |
| **`part`** (part of the household leaves) | leaving the household (leaving the parental home, separation…) | leaving to live with someone |

### Moves at household level

```{r}
#| echo: false

# 2. One row per t-1 household
HH <- PANEL[obs_prev & !is.na(move),
            .(any_move = any(move),        # at least one member moved
              all_move = all(move),        # the whole household moved
              all_dis = all(move_dist),
              all_mun  = all(move_mun),
              all_prov = all(move_prov),
              hh_w     = hh_w_p[1]),
            by = .(year, IDENHOG_p)]

# 3. Weighted shares of households
print(HH[!is.na(hh_w),
         .(any_move = round(100 * weighted.mean(any_move, hh_w), 2),
           all_move = round(100 * weighted.mean(all_move, hh_w), 2),
           all_dis  = round(100 * weighted.mean(all_dis,  hh_w), 2),
           mun      = round(100 * weighted.mean(all_mun,  hh_w), 2),
           prov     = round(100 * weighted.mean(all_prov, hh_w), 2)),
         by = year][order(year)])
```

**All_move** = the entire household moves (defined as in seccion censal change)

**all_dis =** the entire household moves defined as in district change (more robust)

### Comparing with INE data

```{r}
#| echo: false

ine_rates <- INE[nationality == "Total" & sex == "Ambos sexos",
                 .(pop      = n[relation == "Total"],
                   same     = n[relation == "En el mismo municipio"],
                   mun_prov = n[relation == "En distinto municipio y en igual provincia"],
                   prov_ca  = n[relation == "En distinta provincia y en igual comunidad"],
                   other_ca = n[relation == "En distinta comunidad"]),
                 by = .(year, age)]

# Check: the categories add up to the total
stopifnot(ine_rates[, all(pop == same + mun_prov + prov_ca + other_ca)])

# Municipality change = the 3 "distinct" categories; province change = the last 2
ine_rates[, `:=`(ine_mun  = (mun_prov + prov_ca + other_ca) / pop,
                 ine_prov = (prov_ca + other_ca) / pop)]

# ---- 1. National comparison by year ----
comp <- ine_rates[age == "Total", .(year, ine_mun, ine_prov)][rates, on = "year"]
comp[, (c("ine_mun", "ine_prov")) := lapply(.SD, function(x) round(100 * x, 2)),
     .SDcols = c("ine_mun", "ine_prov")]                                   # rates already in %
comp[, `:=`(ratio_mun = round(mun / ine_mun, 2), ratio_prov = round(prov / ine_prov, 2))]
comp[, .(year, mun, ine_mun, ratio_mun, prov, ine_prov, ratio_prov)]

# ---- 2. Comparison by age (same age groups as the INE) ----
age_lab <- c("De 0 a 15 años", "De 16 a 24 años", "De 25 a 34 años", "De 35 a 44 años",
             "De 45 a 54 años", "De 55 a 64 años", "65 y más años")

panel_age <- PANEL[year >= 2021, .(mun  = wm(move_mun,  w),
                                   prov = wm(move_prov, w),
                                   move = wm(move,      w)),
                   by = .(year, age = cut(age, c(-1, 15, 24, 34, 44, 54, 64, 120), labels = age_lab))]
panel_age <- panel_age[!is.na(age)][, age := as.character(age)]

comp_age <- ine_rates[age != "Total", .(year, age, ine_mun, ine_prov)][panel_age, on = .(year, age)]
comp_age[, ratio_mun := mun / ine_mun]
num <- c("mun", "ine_mun", "prov", "ine_prov", "move")
comp_age[, (num) := lapply(.SD, function(x) round(100 * x, 2)), .SDcols = num]
comp_age[, ratio_mun := round(ratio_mun, 2)]
comp_age[order(year, match(age, age_lab))]
```

```{r}
 #| echo: false
PERS <- PANEL[, .(first = min(year), has_gap = any(gap >= 1L, na.rm = TRUE)), by = IDENPER]
share_gap_pers <- PERS[first < 2023L, mean(has_gap)]   # persons who missed >= 1 year
mun_1y  <- PANEL[gap == 0L & !is.na(mun_p), mean(mun != mun_p)]  # 1-year interval
mun_2y  <- PANEL[gap == 1L & !is.na(mun_p), mean(mun != mun_p)] # 2-year interval (one year missed)
pct <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(format(round(100 * x, d), nsmall = d), "%")
```

## Key findings :

- Every year, between 4 and 6% of **people** move (as in change seccion censal) every year /!\\ maybe our criterion of seccion recoding is too strict \<=\> we should consider more moves as recoding. Around 3% change district, 2% change municipality and only 0,7% change province.

- Between 2 and 3% of **households** change district , around 2% change municipality and 0,7% province.

- More than 800.000 movers in total in the panel (more if we consider seccion censal level moving)

- 53% of the moves (district level) are entire households moving whilst 32% of them leave their previous household to live alone (students or separation). 8,6% of moves are people (total households) moving into another household. 4% are people leaving a previous household to integrate a new one

- \~ 3,5% of people aged up to 24 yrs old have moved in the year. This rate goes up to 7% of 24-34 yrs old.

- **Comparing with INE :** the Panel catches \~ 70% of the moves registrated by INE =\> certainly underestimated because the INE uses Padrón info whilst Panel follows people within a sample. Moreover, the most residentially mobile people are less likely to remain within the panel. For example, `r pct(share_gap_pers)` of the persons who entered the panel before 2023 are missing for at least one year before reappearing. Among those who missed one year, `r pct(mun_2y)` live in a different municipality when they reappear, against `r pct(mun_1y)` among persons observed in two consecutive years, **this gap suggests that the most mobile people are the ones the panel follows least well**.

```{r}

new_cols <- setdiff(names(PANEL), cols_start)
new_cols

keep_cols <- c("DISTRITO", "mun", "IDENHOG_p", "gap", "move_sec", "move_dist", "move_mun", "move_prov", "move", "move_dist_ext", "type")

mod_moves <- PANEL[, c("IDENPER", "year", keep_cols), with = FALSE]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(mod_moves, by = c("IDENPER", "year")))   # one row per person-year

tbl <- arrow_table(mod_moves); tbl$metadata$r <- NULL
write_parquet(tbl, bkt$path("panel_hogares/mod_moves.parquet"), compression = "zstd")
```
